DILG DACONO Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www dllq govvh DILG OPINION No. 15 s. 2024 JAN 29 MS. LAI LIM limlairomen@gmail.com Dear Ms. Lim: This has reference to your electronic mail seeking the Department's legal opinion regarding the appointment by a Punong Barangay of the barangay treasurer who is also a beneficiary of Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps). You are seeking legal opinion on the following: I. Is the appointment by the Punong Barangay of a 4Ps beneficiary allowed under the law? 2. Whether the Punong Barangay committed grave abuse when he appointed the Barangay Treasurer knowing fully well that said appointee is a 4Ps beneficiary? 3. Whether the Barangay Treasurer committed dishonesty when she did not disclose to the DSWD about said appointment and kept receiving benefits from the DSWD program? In reply to your we deem it necessary to discuss the qualifications of a Barangay Treasurer. Section 395 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) is instructive, thus: "Section 395. Barangay Treasurer: Appointment, Qualification, Powers and Duties. — (a) The barangay treasurer shall be appointed by the punonq barangay with the concurrence of the maiority of all the sanggunianq baranqay members. The appointment of the barangay treasurer shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. (b) The barangay treasurer shall be of leqal age. a qualified voter, and an actual resident of the barangay concerned. (c) No person shall be appointed baranqay treasurer if he is a sanqgunianq barangay member. a government employee. or a relative of the punonq barangay. within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity. Xxxx" (Emphasis supplied) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

From the foregoing, any actual resident of the barangay concerned may be appointed as Barangay Treasurer provided that he/she is of legal age, a qualified voter and not a sangguniang barangay member, a government employee, or a relative of the punong barangay within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity. Thus, being a 4Ps beneficiary per se does not disqualify him from being appointed as barangay treasurer. A 4Ps beneficiary may still be appointed as barangay treasurer for as long as she he/she possesses all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications as provided by the LGC and with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. As to the second query, we answer in the negative. We reiterate that as long as the punong barangay appointed the barangay treasurer with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members, and that the appointee possesses all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications, the punong barangay acted in accordance with law. As to the final query, it is the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) which selects the qualified household-beneficiaries of the 4Ps using a standardized targeting system. Hence, we advise you to refer the matter to the DSWDI. This opinion is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. It shall be without prejudice to the decisions rendered by competent court or forum. We hope to have sufficiently provided guidance on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, A HORITY OF THE SECRET V OR R. LLAMAS retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Unde OUSELLNJVRlJLLLS-LRALLonasm/clp Copy furnished: FELICITO A.
